idea: Run the live fork Codex TUI and the existing Happy web app against the same Codex-owned, loopback-only Rust Happy session plane, with simultaneous observation/control and no happy-cli or Node happy-server runtime.

candidateDirections.name: Scoped Rust compatibility plane with Socket.IO and direct Codex control
candidateDirections.summary: Add a fork-exclusive Axum + Socketioxide + SQLx/SQLite server crate. Keep codex-happy as a real loopback session client, keep the existing web app on its current Happy HTTP/Socket.IO contract, and route browser RPC calls directly to a serialized in-process CodexControlAdapter.
candidateDirections.primaryRisk: Socketioxide interoperability with the actual browser client
candidateDirections.disconfirmingTest: P0 must prove the real Expo web origin, socket.io-client polling headers, acks, reconnect, and the existing Rust socket client against the intended Rust server stack.

candidateDirections.name: Add a parallel plain-WebSocket transport
candidateDirections.summary: Use a custom WebSocket protocol and modify happy-app, happy-wire, and codex-happy to recreate rooms, acknowledgements, RPC, replay, pagination, reconnect, and auth.
candidateDirections.rejectionReason: Duplicates mature Socket.IO semantics and expands the highest-conflict app sync surface before the first real UI proof.

candidateDirections.name: Direct in-process transcript store plus browser gateway
candidateDirections.summary: Write TUI events directly to a Rust store and expose only a browser gateway, bypassing the session-scoped codex-happy loopback client.
candidateDirections.rejectionReason: Would prove a custom diagnostics gateway rather than the requested real Happy client/server session path.

candidateDirections.name: Full happy-server port or bundled Node sidecar
candidateDirections.summary: Port the broad Node server surface or retain happy-cli/Node as a sidecar.
candidateDirections.rejectionReason: Bundled Node violates the hard requirement; a full port adds unused account/social/push/Redis/multi-replica surface.

recommendedArchitecture.socket: Socketioxide using Socket.IO v4 compatibility at /v1/updates
recommendedArchitecture.control: Serialized CodexControlAdapter backed by AppServerRequestHandle, with authoritative resolution dispositions published back through the local app-server-client event stream
recommendedArchitecture.browserAuth: Versioned local paired-device Ed25519 proof with method/canonical path+query/body hash, freshness, persistent nonce replay rejection, pinned key, exact Origin, and one-time pairing window
recommendedArchitecture.internalAuth: Random 256-bit in-memory capability on every HTTP/socket request
recommendedArchitecture.contentCodec: Explicit LegacyPlainJson codec for message bodies and agent state, preserving the legacy {t:'encrypted',c:<JSON>} message envelope; metadata remains plaintext
recommendedArchitecture.sessionIdentity: Stable tag derived from the primary Codex thread ID
recommendedArchitecture.streaming: Coalesced ephemeral full-text snapshots keyed by item ID; durable final text and tool boundaries

invariants: 1024-entry in-memory replay ring with replay-overflow on uncovered gaps

phasedMilestones.name: Transport/browser/auth spike
phasedMilestones.goal: Prove the intended Rust Socket.IO stack against the actual browser and Rust clients before building persistence.
exitCriteria: Existing Expo web origin reaches loopback with exact-origin CORS.
Browser paired-device headers work over Socket.IO polling.
Existing rust_socketio session client connects over websocket with internal capability.
rpc-call and session-message-range acknowledgements round-trip.
metadata/state CAS acknowledgement shapes round-trip.
update/reconnect/lastSeenSeq/replay-overflow behavior is proven.
Signed query tampering and nonce replay fail closed.
No browser WebSocket custom-header assumption remains.
phasedMilestones.stopCondition: A substantial Engine.IO/Socket.IO reimplementation would be required.

phasedMilestones.name: Native Rust server and real web compatibility
phasedMilestones.goal: Implement the scoped compatibility server, local auth/codec/identity, direct control adapter, and small additive app/wire changes.
exitCriteria: Existing web UI pairs through its existing server screen.
Exactly one real Codex session is listed and opened.
A TUI-origin prompt and output appear in web.
An idle browser message starts a real turn.
Browser reconnect retains durable state without duplication.
Negative auth tests fail closed.

phasedMilestones.name: Same-machine dual-control dogfood
phasedMilestones.goal: Prove simultaneous terminal/browser control of one live Codex thread.
exitCriteria: Alternating terminal and browser turns.
Active-turn steering from the opposite surface.
Idle-start race loses no message.
Coalesced assistant streaming and tool boundaries appear on both.
Approve/deny from each surface.
First-answer-wins returns Applied then AlreadyResolved/Stale.
Interrupt from each surface.
Browser reconnect, /remote off/on, and an idle fully-consumed fixed-port restart preserve one session/history.
/remote off during a pending approval detaches web control without auto-denying the live TUI approval.
Process/port evidence proves no happy-cli or Node happy-server runtime.

phasedMilestones.name: Release and later transports
phasedMilestones.goal: Package only after local proof; then separately harden remote/tablet transports.
exitCriteria: Production feature/documentation and auto-attach are ready.
Remote-grade encryption and transport threat model are complete before LAN/public/tablet exposure.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: The existing Happy web UI, not a toy client, pairs with the embedded Rust server and lists exactly one session for the live primary Codex thread.

Terminal-origin and browser-origin user messages are each rendered exactly once on both surfaces, using happy:<localId> client IDs plus a server-enforced codex-origin: internal localId namespace to suppress both echo boundaries; browser messages receive message-consumption only after Codex accepts them.

A browser message while idle uses TurnStart; while active it uses TurnSteer; all requests target the TUI root thread, no second Codex thread/process is created, and steer/completion and start/start races lose no input.
Assistant text streams to web as coalesced full snapshots, final text is durable, and tool start/end events are visible on both surfaces.
Approval/deny is available from both surfaces with authoritative first-answer-wins outcomes and no false success for a second response.
Interrupt from browser cancels pending approvals then interrupts the active turn; TUI interrupt is reflected in web.
Message sequence, update cursor, localId idempotency, reconnect replay, overflow recovery, CAS, and range pagination match the existing app contract.
The listener binds only to 127.0.0.1 and every non-OPTIONS request/socket is authenticated by paired-device proof or the in-memory internal capability.
The native-local backend never invokes happy, reads ~/.happy discovery/credentials, starts a Node server, or falls back to the legacy daemon.

Structured logs and Windows process/port inventory prove the session-plane listener belongs to the Codex PID; no Node process owns or hosts the Happy session plane, and unrelated Node tooling is classified separately.
/remote off/on and fixed-port restart/resume reopen the same stable thread-tagged session rather than creating duplicates.
Default-off gating preserves vanilla Codex behavior byte-for-byte when the feature/backend is not selected.

settledDecisions: Implement a scoped compatibility server rather than the full happy-server.
Use a separate fork-overlay codex-happy-server crate.
Route browser RPC directly to an in-process control adapter.
Keep browser user messages on the real Happy HTTP/update/session-client path.
Add an explicit paired-device auth mode and a distinct local invite; leave the existing Cloudflare-backed public invite strict and unchanged.
Use an explicit local plaintext codec and retain legacy encrypted codecs.
Derive the Happy session tag from the primary Codex thread ID.
Persist message/update sequence and replay nonces in SQLite.
Default to an ephemeral loopback port with a fixed-port test override.
Stop the embedded server immediately on /remote off.
Require browser streaming snapshots before claiming P2 success.
Defer all remote/tablet transports until local acceptance passes.

openDecisions.decision: Exact UI rendering of one transient streaming item
openDecisions.recommendation: Use the existing message surface and static replacement; if a genuine presentation judgment remains, assign only that narrow question to an Opus 4.8 UI sub-agent.
Two minutes and one successful enrollment, reopened explicitly.

openDecisions.decision: Product behavior after restart when the default ephemeral port changes
openDecisions.recommendation: Re-import a fresh invite in Phase 1; use a fixed port for deterministic dogfood; do not add a daemon merely for rendezvous.

openDecisions.decision: Aggregation of multiple simultaneous Codex TUI processes
openDecisions.recommendation: Out of scope; one embedded server per live TUI is correct for this proof.

blockers.description: Socketioxide compatibility has source plausibility but no executed real-browser proof.
Current approval resolution cannot authoritatively distinguish first from second response.
Current web plaintext and Rust ciphertext handling are incompatible for both message bodies and agent state.
Current mapping drops local user messages and token deltas.

reuse: approval payload mapping and cancel-before-interrupt behavior
Happy session envelope and HTTP/Socket.IO contracts
paired-device signed-request format and test vectors
default-off RemoteSession and later RemoteAutoAttach gates
replace: generic socket-room RPC bridge for local control
blanket approval cancellation on remote detach while the live TUI remains available

conflictSurface.risk: medium rebase surface; keep to marked seams

paths: packages/happy-app/sources/text/_default.ts and locale files only if copy changes
conflictSurface.risk: sync.ts is a known manual-three-way hotspot; keep changes surgical
must explicitly document local plaintext and Node-web-tooling exception

securityReview.verdict: GO for loopback-only local proof; NO-GO for remote exposure
requiredControls: exact Host for all traffic and exact Origin for paired browser traffic
freshness and persistent nonce replay rejection
one-time pairing window and constant-time secret comparison
fail-closed native backend with no legacy fallback
negative HTTP and Socket.IO auth inventory tests
acceptedLocalLimitations: Browser device seed is in localStorage and is exposed by same-origin XSS.
Conversation JSON and agent state are plaintext in the local SQLite database.
Same-user malware/admin access is out of scope.
remoteReleaseBlockers: browser websocket challenge auth or equivalent

hiddenDependencyReview.verdict: No hidden happy-cli or Node happy-server dependency in the recommended session path.
forbidden: Node child process for the session plane
allowed: Node/Expo process used solely to build or serve the existing Happy web UI during development
Unrelated Node tooling or model-invoked Node tool processes whose command lines are classified and which do not own or host the session plane
verification: source invariants for forbidden legacy paths
full process command-line inventory in P2 evidence
